BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION

     IN THE MATTER OF THE APPLICATION OF                               )
     EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY FOR                                      ) Docket No. 25-00082-UT
     REVISION OF ITS RETAIL ELECTRIC RATES                             )
     PURSUANT TO ADVICE NOTICE NO. 317                                 )

                            ORDER DENYING MOTION TO DISMISS

          THIS MATTER comes before hearing examiners Keven Gedko and Nicholas Rossi,

upon the filing of the City of Las Cruces’s (“CLC”) Verified Motion to Dismiss El Paso

Electric Company’s (“EPE”) Application for Revision of Retail Electric Rates (“Motion to

Dismiss”), EPE’s Response in Opposition to CLC’s Motion to Dismiss (“EPE’s Response”),

and CLC’s Motion for Leave to Reply to EPE’s Response (“Motion for Leave to Reply”).

          For the reasons stated below, the Hearing Examiners grant CLC’s Motion for Leave to

Reply, and deny CLC’s Motion to Dismiss.

               I.   PROCEDURAL BACKGROUND1

          1.        On March 27, 2026, EPE filed its Application for Revision of Retail Electric

Rates (“Application”) seeking revision of its New Mexico retail electric rates pursuant to

Advice Notice No. 317. EPE’s Application asserted that it was filed in accordance with

17.9.530 NMAC (“Rule 530”), and that it provided a fully allocated cost of service study based

on cost data from a twelve-month Base Period ending September 30, 2025, and a twelve-month

Historical Test Year Period adjusted pursuant to Rule 530.2

          2.        On June 30, 2026, CLC filed its Motion to Dismiss, in which it asked the



1
 This section summarizes relevant background. The full electronic record of this proceeding is available at
https://e360.prc.nm.gov/portal/public/.
2
    Application (March 27, 2026) at 6; Direct Testimony of George Novela at 6:9-10.
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Denying Motion to Dismiss                             Docket No. 25-00082-UT


Commission to reject EPE’s Application “pursuant to Rule 17.1.3.9 NMAC on the grounds

that [EPE] has mixed an unspecified Future Test Year Period rate application with a Historical

Test Period Rate filing, without explanation, justification, and the base period, test period,

linkage, and future test period data required by Rule 17.1.3 NMAC.”3

           3.       On July 8, 2026, Hearing Examiner Jocelyn Barrett issued the Order Requiring

EPE and Staff Response to Motion to Dismiss and Extending Deadlines for Responses, which

required EPE and Staff, and permitted other parties, to file a written response addressing

CLC’s Motion to Dismiss on or before July 21, 2026.

           4.       Subsequently, on July 16, 2026, Hearing Examiner Jocelyn Barrett issued the

Sua Sponte Order Vacating Procedural Schedule, Tolling Pending Deadlines, and Requiring

the Filing of an Amended Application (“Sua Sponte Order”). The Sua Sponte Order vacated

the hearing and procedural schedule previously established, tolled all pending motion and other

deadlines, and required EPE to file, within twenty-one calendar days, a single amended and

restated application and complete supporting filing package.4 The Sua Sponte Order also

required Staff to file a Completeness Report, within seven calendar days after EPE filed its

amended application, stating whether the amended application and supporting materials were

sufficiently complete, coherent, internally consistent, and technically usable to permit this

proceeding to continue.5

           5.       On August 6, 2026, EPE filed its Amended Application for Revision of Retail



3
    Motion to Dismiss (June 30, 2026) at 18.

    Sua Sponte Order (July 16, 2026) at 1, and Decretal ¶¶ A through E.

Electric Rates (“Amended Application”), which states, “This Amended Application

supersedes and replaces the original Application and should be treated as a single integrated

and comprehensive filing.”6 EPE’s Amended Application asserts that it is filed in accordance

with the requirements of Rule 530, and that it provides a fully allocated cost of service study

based on cost data from a twelve-month Base Period ending September 30, 2025, and a twelve-

month Historical Test Year Period adjusted pursuant to Rule 530 and ending on September 30,

2025.7

            6.     On August 13, 2026, Staff filed its Completeness Report, which concluded that

EPE’s Amended Application is “sufficiently complete to allow this matter to proceed,” and

EPE “has filed a complete application sufficient for and capable of litigation through the

administrative adversarial process.”8

            7.     On August 27, 2026, the Hearing Examiners issued their Order Establishing

Revised Procedural Schedule and Addressing Outstanding Motions (“August 27th Order”), in

which the Hearing Examiners found that EPE’s Amended Application is sufficiently complete

to allow this matter to proceed.9

            8.     The August 27th Order established that EPE, and any other party besides CLC,

would have an opportunity to respond to CLC’s Motion to Dismiss on or before September 8,

2026. The August 27th Order also vacated the previously established requirement that Staff

respond to CLC’s Motion to Dismiss.

6
    Amended Application (August 6, 2026) at 1.
7
    Id. at 9.
8
    Completeness Report (August 13, 2026) at 7-8.
9
    August 27th Order (August 27, 2026) ¶ 5.

Order Denying Motion to Dismiss                             Docket No. 25-00082-UT


            9.        On September 8, 2026, EPE filed EPE’s Response, which opposes CLC’s

Motion to Dismiss. No other party filed a response to CLC’s Motion to Dismiss.

            10.       On September 21, 2026, CLC filed its Motion for Leave to Reply, which

requests leave to reply to EPE’s Response, and requests that the Commission accept CLC’s

Reply to EPE’s Response (“CLC’s Reply”).

             II.      CLC’s MOTION FOR LEAVE TO REPLY

            11.       CLC seeks leave to submit CLC’s Reply “in order to clarify the focus of the

City’s Motion to Dismiss and to address [EPE]’s interpretations of statutes, rules, and case law

that [CLC] believes are mistaken,”10 and because CLC believes that acceptance of CLC’s

Reply will assist the Commission in determining whether to grant CLC’s Motion to Dismiss.11

            12.       In its Motion for Leave to Reply, CLC communicates EPE’s position on CLC’s

Motion for Leave to Reply as follows: “EPE states [EPE] ‘opposes the motion for leave to

reply because the proposed reply contains new arguments to which EPE has not had an

opportunity to respond.”12

            13.       1.2.2.12(C)(1)d) NMAC establishes that replies to responses to motions “shall

not be filed without leave of the commission or presiding officer,” and “[r]eplies to responses

shall be filed within thirteen (13) days of service of the response, or such other time period as

the commission or presiding officer may prescribe.”

            14.       The Hearing Examiners did not prescribe a time period for the filing of replies



10
     Motion for Leave to Reply (September 21, 2026) at 3, ¶ 8.
11
     Id. at 4, ¶ 6.
12
     Id. at 4, ¶ 8.

                                                       -4-
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Denying Motion to Dismiss                             Docket No. 25-00082-UT


to EPE’s Response, and therefore the deadline to file replies was September 21, 2026. CLC

met that deadline by filing its Motion for Leave to Reply, accompanied by CLC’s Reply, on

September 21, 2026.

           15.     CLC’s Motion to Dismiss was filed prior to the filing of EPE’s Amended

Application, and EPE asserts that its Amended Application “supersedes and replaces the

original Application and should be treated as a single integrated and comprehensive filing.”13

Further, arguments in EPE’s Response refer to and rely upon EPE’s Amended Application.14

           16.     It is therefore reasonable that CLC be permitted to reply to EPE’s Response, in

order to ensure CLC has the opportunity to clarify its arguments with reference to and reliance

upon the Amended Application.

           17.     Hence, CLC’s Motion for Leave to Reply should be granted.

           III.    CLC’s MOTION TO DISMISS

           18.     CLC’s Motion to Dismiss asks the Commission to reject EPE’s Application

“pursuant to Rule 17.1.3.9 NMAC on the grounds that the Company has mixed an unspecified

Future Test Year Period rate application with a Historical Test Period Rate filing, without

explanation, justification, and the base period, test period, linkage, and future test period data

required by Rule 17.1.3 NMAC.”15 CLC’s Reply states that the basis of CLC’s Motion to

Dismiss is that EPE’s “rate application amounts to a future test year period filing without the

information required by Rule 17.1.3 NMAC,”16 and further states, “[CLC]’s Motion to Dismiss

13
     Amended Application at 1.
14
     See EPE’s Response at 8, 9-10, 14.
15
     Motion to Dismiss at 18.
16
     CLC’s Reply (September 21, 2026) at 1.

                                                  -5-
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Denying Motion to Dismiss                             Docket No. 25-00082-UT


is based on [EPE]’s failure to comply with Rule 17.1.3 NMAC and, thus, falls under the

category of ‘patently deficient in form.’”17

            19.    After reviewing multiple Commission orders that have addressed motions to

dismiss filed in other dockets, CLC asserts that motions to dismiss are addressed by the

Commission by testing “whether a filing is either patently deficient in form or a nullity in

substance.”18

            20.    CLC then states: “The essence of the City’s Motion to Dismiss is that utilities,

including EPE, must comply with the form of filings for rate applications specified by

Commission rules,”19 and, “[CLC]’s Motion to Dismiss was based on [EPE]’s original

Application being patently deficient in form in its non-compliance with Rule 17.1.3 NMAC

governing future test period rate filings. The City’s Motion to Dismiss applies with equal force

to EPE’s Amended Application. The Commission clearly has authority to dismiss a rate

application that does not comply with explicit filing requirements set by constitution, statute,

or rule.”20

            21.    For its part, EPE states:

            [CLC] asks the Commission to throw out EPE’s entire rate case. To obtain that
            relief, the City must show that EPE’s filing is ‘patently deficient in form or a
            nullity in substance,’ meaning that under no provable set of facts could EPE be
            entitled to any rate relief. The inquiry is legal, not evidentiary. To evaluate such
            a claim, the Commission accepts the applicant’s factual presentation as true,
            does not weigh the merits, and does not dismiss a case because an intervenor



17
     Id. at 3.
18
     Id. at 2-4.
19
     Id. at 5.
20
     Id. at 6.

                                                    -6-
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Denying Motion to Dismiss                             Docket No. 25-00082-UT


           thinks the applicant will lose a contested issue.21

           22.      Hence, EPE and CLC agree that CLC’s Motion to Dismiss must show that

EPE’s filing is “patently deficient in form or a nullity in substance.” However, CLC and EPE

disagree on the application of that standard.

           23.      CLC asserts that a filing is patently deficient in form or a nullity in substance if

it fails to comply with explicit filing requirements set by constitution, statute, or rule. EPE

asserts that a filing is patently deficient in form or a nullity in substance if, under no provable

set of facts could the applicant be entitled to any relief.

           24.      CLC’s Reply argues against EPE’s assertion that “patently deficient in form or

a nullity in substance” means that an application is of a form such that under no provable set

of facts could the applicant be entitled to any relief.22

           25.      So, it might appear that the Hearing Examiners need to address EPE and CLC’s

competing arguments regarding how to determine whether an application is “patently deficient

in form or a nullity in substance,” in order to rule upon CLC’s Motion to Dismiss. But that is

not so.

           26.      As detailed above, CLC reiterates multiple times that it bases its Motion to

Dismiss on the foundation that EPE’s Application, and Amended Application, are deficient in

form due to non-compliance with Rule 17.1.3 NMAC. And though CLC does, in one instance,

state that EPE’s Application and Amended Application are “inconsistent with Commission




21
     EPE’s Response at 1. (Internal citations omitted.)
22
     CLC’s Reply at 6-7.

                                                          -7-
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Denying Motion to Dismiss                             Docket No. 25-00082-UT


rules for the filing of a historical test period or a future test period rate application,” 23 CLC

does not present arguments for how EPE’s Application or Amended Application might fail to

comply with explicit filing requirements for the filing of a historical test period application,

which are set by 17.9.530 NMAC.

            27.    Yet, EPE’s Application and Amended Application both explicitly establish that

EPE is seeking relief under the “Historical Test Year Period” requirements of Rule 530,24

adjusted pursuant to Rule 530, as described in Rule 17.9.530.7(S)(1) NMAC.25

            28.    It follows that CLC’s argument to dismiss EPE’s Application or Amended

Application, on the basis that it fails to comply with explicit filing requirements set by

constitution, statute, or rule, would need to show that EPE’s Application or Amended

Application fails to comply with the explicit filing requirements of 17.9.530 NMAC. CLC’s

Motion to Dismiss, and CLC’s Reply, instead argue that EPE’s Application and Amended

Application fail to meet the filing requirements of 17.1.3 NMAC.

            29.    Hence, even if the dispute regarding the standard for determining whether an

application is “patently deficient in form or a nullity in substance” were resolved in CLC’s


23
     Id. ¶ 8.
24
  For clarity, please note that 17.9.530.7(S)(2) NMAC identifies a filing for a “future test year period” that is
not the test year period that is identified in Rule 17.1.3 NMAC, the latter of which is the basis of CLC’s
Motion to Dismiss. 17.9.530.7(S)(2) identifies a future test year period that means the twelve (12) consecutive
months following the last day of the applicant utility's twelve (12) months of actual experience [otherwise the
Base Period] adjusted for known and measurable changes and/or estimates based on projections for which
period the applicant utility's total revenue requirements shall be determined. 17.1.3 NMAC, and 17.1.3.2 in
particular, instead identify a future test year “where the future test year period is not the 12 consecutive months
following the last day of the base period.” Hence, not only is EPE not applying for relief under a future test
year period as defined in 17.1.3 NMAC, but is also not applying for a future test year period defined in
17.9.530 NMAC.
25
     Application (March 27, 2026) at 6; Direct Testimony of George Novela at 6:9-10; Amended Application at
9.

                                                        -8-
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Denying Motion to Dismiss                             Docket No. 25-00082-UT


favor, CLC’s Motion to Dismiss fails to provide arguments and support that would meet that

standard.26

          30.     In a demonstration of this, CLC states:

          As explained throughout the City’s Motion to Dismiss, the Company’s mixing
          of future (or post-test-period) resource additions and their costs with historical
          data about loads and the usage of other generation and storage resources that are
          not being treated as “dedicated” is contrary to Rule 17.1.3 NMAC’s demanding
          requirements for a future test period rate application filing. Once EPE decided
          to include these future resources, it was bound by the Commission’s rules to
          take on the burden of making a dual showing: that of presenting a historical test
          year filing with linkage data connecting the historical data to the future test year
          filing which defines the revenue requirement and rate design.27

Reviewing this statement, the Hearing Examiners note that CLC is incorrect in asserting that

EPE is “bound by the Commission’s rules to take on the burden … of presenting … linkage

data connecting the historical data to the future test year filing.” As reviewed above, EPE has

filed its Application and Amended Application under Rule 17.9.530, which does not require

the filing of linkage data. Instead, under a “Historical Test Year Period” filing under

17.9.530.7(S)(1), the "Historical Test Year Period" which establishes the utility’s total revenue

requirement is developed by applying to the Base Period “all proper adjustments, such as

annualizations and known and measurable changes.” CLC’s concerns regarding the proper

accounting for post-test-period resource additions, and their relationship to test period loads,

are therefore properly the subject of testimony and litigation regarding “proper adjustments,

such as known and measurable changes” to the Base Period defined in EPE’s Application and


26
  As EPE similarly stated in its Response: “Because EPE filed a historical test year case, 17.1.3 NMAC does
not apply, no “linkage data” was required, and 17.1.3.9 NMAC supplies no basis for rejecting the filing.”
EPE’s Response at 10.
27
     CLC’s Reply at 11.

                                                     -9-
                 BEFORE THE NEW MEXICO PUBLIC REGULATION COMMISSION
Order Denying Motion to Dismiss                             Docket No. 25-00082-UT


Amended Application, filed under 17.9.530 NMAC.

      31.    In sum, CLC’s Motion to Dismiss argues that an application should be dismissed

when it does not meet filing requirements, EPE’s Application and Amended Application have

been filed under 17.9.530 NMAC, CLC’s Motion to Dismiss does not address the filing

requirements of 17.9.530 NMAC, and therefore CLC’s Motion to Dismiss should be denied.

      IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED:

      A.     CLC’s Motion for Leave to Reply is GRANTED.

      B.     CLC’s Reply, attached to CLC’s Motion for Leave to Reply as Exhibit 4, is

ACCEPTED as being filed into this Docket No. 25-00082-UT on September 21, 2026.

      C.     CLC’s Motion to Dismiss is DENIED.

ISSUED under the seal of the Commission at Santa Fe, New Mexico, on September 28, 2026.
